title: Immutable runtime shims and slim builder to cut CI latency and layer churn
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: CI job times and cache-miss rates have regressed over the last 9 months as more language runtimes and tooling were layered into monolithic Docker bases. We see a ~28% median increase in job wall time for language-runner images and frequent invalidation of downstream images when developer toolchain changes. Goal: Reduce CI latency and image push size by splitting builder/runtime responsibilities, adopting immutable runtime shims, and enabling content-addressable/reusable build layers via BuildKit remote cache. Approach:

1) Split current monolithic Dockerfiles into two artifacts: a slim 'runtime-shim' image (only OS libs, runtime binaries, pinned openssl/zlib, runtime shims) and a 'builder' image that contains compilers, linters, test tooling, and ephemeral build-time deps. Runtime shims are immutable and versioned independently.
2) Move developer toolchain upgrades into the builder image CI path so changes do not invalidate runtime-shim layers.
3) Enable BuildKit with a remote content-addressable cache (CAS) for the builder stage and configure TTL-based retention for rarely-used layers.
4) Adopt multi-stage builds with named stages and explicit COPY --from=builder patterns to avoid copying unnecessary files and to make layer boundaries stable.
5) Introduce a small shim compatibility test (binary check + libc/symbol surface) in the release pipeline to ensure runtime-shim upgrades are safe for downstream services.
6) Provide a migration guide and automation to rebase service Dockerfiles to the new pattern, including a codemod for common repo layouts.

Why this is different from prior work: instead of converging to a single large base image, this design intentionally fragments build-time and run-time artifacts to reduce entropy and cross-repo rebuilds. It complements existing remote-cache efforts by providing more stable layer anchors (the runtime shims).
acceptance_criteria: Median CI build time for language-runner images reduced by at least 20% within two weeks of rollout
Remote BuildKit cache hit rate for builder stages >= 70% for active repos
Average pushed image size for runtime-shims < 120MB gzipped
All service Dockerfiles migrated or on a migration plan with automation for 90% of active repos by pipeline-side rollout
Compatibility shim tests added to release pipeline and passing for 100% of runtime-shim updates
rollout_plan: 1) PoC: Implement runtime-shim + slim builder for 2 low-risk services (search-ingest, experiments-runner) and measure. 2) Validate BuildKit remote cache integration and TTL policy in staging. 3) Create codemod and run automated PRs for migration across 10 medium-traffic repos. 4) Ramp to all repos, monitoring cache hit rates and image push bandwidth. 5) Deprecate legacy monolithic base images and provide final notices. Rollout timeline: PoC (2 weeks) -> Migration wave 1 (3 weeks) -> Full ramp (6 weeks).
